recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not edit dormant core SupplyRequest or SupplyDelivery files for this issue; if OO wants additional SupplyRequest wording changes, make them in the current OO Incubator source or open a new core issue for active cross-resource guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-24936 was Published/Persuasive for R5 by OO. It requested Scope and Usage and Boundaries and Relationships updates for healthcare-product resources including BiologicallyDerivedProduct, Device, DeviceDefinition, DeviceUseRequest/DeviceUseStatement successors, Substance, and SupplyRequest according to the attached clean/markup documents and Jira comment corrections.
initial_application: The issue was applied through multiple historical commits. The February 2020 Device and DeviceUseStatement commits a7f2575daae7bbacd9a22ea439c7ec35a4784f96 and 8e3a45ff180909573902419b71ea67f57d7663c2 explicitly listed FHIR-24936. Commit 578361a9000ef12bb67e86de2e5fb27ea52bd79a then changed BiologicallyDerivedProduct, DeviceDefinition, DeviceRequest, Substance, SupplyDelivery, and SupplyRequest source files for FHIR-24936.
additional_context: FHIR-27941 and OO HCP minutes recorded that FHIR-24936 had not been fully applied, particularly for SupplyRequest; that follow-up clarification is already represented on the combined branch. Later related audits and fixes on the combined branch address DeviceRequest/SupplyRequest boundary history, SupplyRequest definition migration, and the DeviceDefinition packaging sentence that a broad scope rewrite had overwritten. Current source/fhir.ini keeps BiologicallyDerivedProduct, Device, DeviceDefinition, DeviceRequest, DeviceUsage, and Substance active, but commit 3b38b80cf23f9cbb306fab8fcedb293315478c32 removed SupplyRequest and SupplyDelivery from the active core build and redirected to the OO Incubator.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current active core source already conveys the requested distinctions for biologically derived products, device kind versus instance usage, patient-focused DeviceRequest, report-focused DeviceUsage, and Substance as an instance material distinct from SubstanceDefinition and NutritionProduct. The retained SupplyRequest files still show the FHIR-24936 inventory-management and non-patient-specific wording, but SupplyRequest is no longer an active core resource.

related_jiras.note: Follow-up Published issue explicitly noted FHIR-24936 was not fully applied for SupplyRequest and resolved the DeviceRequest versus SupplyRequest clarification; already represented on the combined branch.
Earlier DeviceUseRequest/SupplyRequest boundary decision helps interpret the patient-focused DeviceRequest distinction; already represented on the combined branch.
Later DeviceDefinition packaging issue restored a scope sentence overwritten by the broad FHIR-24936 DeviceDefinition rewrite; already represented on the combined branch.
Later SupplyRequest definition migration confirms SupplyRequest wording and ownership history; already represented on the combined branch.
